issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s attestation of a written subletting letter can establish both prior written consent to the subtenancy and written notice of that particular subtenancy, entitling the subtenant to protection against eviction under a decree against the head tenant.
material_facts: The premises were let to a firm, which sublet them to the appellant firm; the courts below found that the appellant firm was a subtenant, not a direct tenant.
The head tenant gave the appellant a letter confirming the subletting, and the landlord attested that letter.
The landlord later obtained an ex parte eviction decree against the head tenant and sought to execute it against the appellant, which occupied the premises.
The appellant relied on the landlord’s written involvement in the subletting to claim protection, although it had not established compliance through a separate prescribed notice.
issues.conclusion: The written letter attested by the landlord evidenced both the landlord’s prior consent and his written knowledge of the particular subtenancy. The appellant was entitled to protection and could not be evicted in execution of the decree against the head tenant.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 17 and 18 of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, a subtenant may become a tenant directly under the landlord when the statutory conditions are met. The essential requirement is written evidence of the landlord’s prior consent to the subtenancy and written evidence that the landlord knew of that particular subtenancy; the evidence may be contained in one document or several, and no prescribed form is indispensable. The Court construed the Act purposively to advance its protection against unreasonable eviction, applying the principle that legislative intention and statutory purpose may warrant a construction beyond a merely literal reading. It relied on Hawkins v. Gathercole; Comet Radio Vision Services v. Farnell Trand Borg; Seaford Court Estates Ltd. v. Asher; Rugby Joint Water Board v. Foottit; K.P. Varghese v. I.T.O.; State Bank of Travancore v. Mohd. M. Khan; Som Prakash Rekhi v. Union of India; Ravula Subba Rao v. C.I.T.; Govindlal v. Market Committee; and Babaji Kondaji v. Nasik Merchants Coop. Bank. Rule 21 and Form E of the Delhi Rent Control Rules, 1959, prescribe the form of notice, but the majority held that the written attested letter here satisfied the substance of the requirements. Justice Khalid agreed with the result but stated that the statutory conditions should normally be strictly complied with and regarded the case as exceptional because of the landlord’s and head tenant’s conduct.

predicates.occupant_is_subtenant_of_evicted_tenant: The occupant took the premises by subletting from the tenant against whom the eviction decree was obtained.
predicates.subtenant_challenges_execution_of_evicti: The subtenant objected to the execution of an eviction decree that would remove it from the premises.
predicates.eviction_decree_is_against_head_tenant_n: The eviction decree was obtained against the head tenant and not against the subtenant.
predicates.landlord_attested_written_subletting_let: The head tenant gave the subtenant a written letter confirming the subletting, and the landlord attested that letter.

issues.definition: When a subtenant challenges execution of a decree against the head tenant and the landlord attested the written letter confirming the subletting, the subtenant is protected from eviction under that decree.
